From: Sarah Coleman <sarah.coleman@pioneerinsure.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API p95: temporary measurement window question

Hi Lauren,

We’re approaching our policy-driven migration (cutover scheduled for 2026-07-04) and are digging into contract operational details for the hosted API p50/p95 commitments. During a dry-run yesterday we observed multiple short, intense bursts tied to a scheduled batch sync from an upstream partner. The instantaneous spikes are creating p95 noise in the 24-hour measurement bucket.

Ask: would Redwood consider a temporary measurement resampling (or short grace window) for p95 during our cutover week? Specifically, PioneerInsure is proposing: 
- a 72-hour resampling window (i.e., allow one 72h window to be used to smooth ephemeral burst artifacts)
- requirement to provide telemetry (traffic profile + retention of request ids) for audit
- opt-in canary traffic to validate behavior

We’re happy to provide the burst profile and test plan. This is time-sensitive—if we can land a short-term operational agreement it will prevent unnecessary credit requests after a noisy cutover.

Thanks,
Sarah Coleman
Director, Platform Engineering
PioneerInsure

Sarah / Lauren — quick engineering read: the phenomena you describe (short, high-amplitude bursts pushing tail percentiles in a 24h bucket) is familiar. We can offer a controlled, temporary resampling policy with the following guardrails: 

- Scope: one 72-hour resampling window, applied only during the defined cutover period (start/end times in UTC).
- Evidence required: per-request IDs, region tag, sequence id for correlated upstream batches, and 30 days of trace logs retained.
- Metric semantics: we will continue to compute p50/p95 as usual, but for the agreed 72-hour window we will apply a rolling median filter for transient spikes (only used for contractual measurement, not for alerting).
- Controls: telemetry checklist (attached) must be complete and validated in our staging environment; we require a canary traffic tranche (1–5% of production) for 24 hours prior to enabling the window.
- Fallback: automatic rollback to standard measurement if error rates >0.5% or if KV-cache warmup anomalies occur.

Operationally, this is best implemented as an explicit measurement addendum (one paragraph) and an internal ops ticket that enumerates the exact UTC window. Ben — can you confirm whether this approach has commercial implications (credits, SLA notes)?

I’ve attached a telemetry checklist that lists the exact artifacts we need. If Pioneer can deliver that and the canary results, we’ll approve the temporary resampling.

— Rishi
